data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 't-r-y', meaning to strike or fight. Mutair is a name for the brave and fearless, one who strikes at injustice with unwavering courage. The name Mutair carries the meaning “Intrepid, Fearless” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mutair usually hope their child will grow to embody intrepid, fearless and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of courage and resilience in the face of adversity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mutair total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_urdu.name: مطیر

historical_references.reference: Mutair ibn Ja'far Al-Kadhim was a prominent Shia Imam and scholar born in 813 AD in Baghdad, Iraq. He was known for his deep knowledge of Hadith and Fiqh, and he served as a teacher and advisor to various caliphs and rulers throughout his life. Mutair was particularly revered by the Twelver Shia community for his piety and devotion to the religious cause.

Mutair ibn Abdullah Al-Hassan was a renowned Arab poet and scholar who lived during the Umayyad and Abbasid periods, around the 8th century AD. He is best known for his collection of poetry, which includes descriptions of the natural world and reflections on the passage of time and the human condition. Mutair's poetry was influential in shaping the literary traditions of the Arabic language and continues to be studied and appreciated today.
